clue.text: Get your leg over favourite bike

blocks.note: the favourite is the best-liked one
a bike is something you ride; a ride is slang for a bicycle or motorbike

explanation.surface: A cheeky instruction to swing a leg over your favourite bicycle, with a saucy double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestride something is to sit astride it, one leg either side, as a rider mounts a horse or bike.

clue.text: Spooner's sweet stall at school makes problem for the dentist

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of two words, so the starts of the two words found here change places

blocks.note: tuck is schoolchildren's slang for sweets and snacks, and a booth is a stall; swapping the opening sounds gives the answer

explanation.surface: A school tuck shop leads, unsurprisingly, to work for the dentist.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuck is British school slang for sweets and snacks, as in a tuck shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck tooth is a protruding upper front tooth, the kind of malocclusion a dentist or orthodontist is asked to correct.

clue.text: Drunkard outside pub is argumentative type

indicators.note: one thing standing outside another wraps around it, so the drunkard's word encloses the rest

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
PH is the map abbreviation for public house
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk propping up the outside of a pub picks fights with anyone passing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sophist argues cleverly but speciously, so he is a quarrelsome, disputatious person.

clue.text: Changing speed when cycling west of Ulan Bator

indicators.note: on a map the west is the left side, so only the leftmost letter of the word Ulan is taken
cycling sends letters round in a loop, so the last letter moves round to the front

blocks.note: the westernmost, leftmost letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notes the pace altering as they cycle on the western edge of the Mongolian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: U joined to BATOR gives UBATOR; moving its last letter round to the front gives RUBATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubato is the musical device of freely speeding up and slowing down within a phrase, so it is a change of tempo.

clue.text: Slight tantrum after i-Pad's removed

indicators.note: something removed has been shifted from its spot, suggesting these letters are moved into a new arrangement
after places the tantrum's word second, behind the rearranged tablet letters

blocks.note: the letters of the tablet's name with its S
a tantrum is a fit of rage

explanation.surface: A child throws a small tantrum after having an iPad taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' looks like an adjective modifying tantrum but is the verb meaning to belittle; RAGE goes after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To slight someone is to treat them dismissively, which is what disparaging them does.

clue.text: Dirty old town reflected times

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: burg is an old word for a town or borough
by means times in multiplication, as in four by six

explanation.surface: A grimy old town is mirrored in the newspaper, perhaps The Times, of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the song Dirty Old Town; 'times' reads as a newspaper but means multiplied by.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grubby is soiled with grime, an everyday synonym for dirty.

clue.text: Sign up on ship saw sailor leap, clearing the sides

indicators.note: clearing away the sides strips off both outer letters, leaving the middle of the word leap

blocks.note: to get something is to see or understand it, as in 'I got it'
OS stands for ordinary seaman
the inner letters of the word

explanation.surface: Having signed on to a ship, someone watched a sailor jump clear over the rails.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to sea is to take up life as a sailor, which is what joining a ship's crew means.

clue.text: You said shoplift a gardening store? Not guilty

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word you is wanted only for its sound

blocks.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word
to nab is to steal, informally
taken as written
a garden shed stores tools

explanation.surface: Accused of stealing a garden shed, the suspect pleads not guilty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not guilty' reads as a verdict but means feeling no guilt, unembarrassed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unabashed means without shame or embarrassment, so someone unabashed feels no guilt about what they did.

clue.text: Bank's first home loan switched to match others

indicators.note: first asks only for the opening letter of the word Bank
switched means the two words home and loan trade places before being written down

blocks.note: the opening letter
at home means in
to lend is to make a loan; loan is also used as a verb

explanation.surface: A bank's first-time home loan was switched over to match competitors' terms.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend in is to fit with one's surroundings so as not to stand out, matching those around you.

clue.text: Third in race winning prize

indicators.note: third in asks for the letter in third position of the word race

blocks.note: the third letter
to be up is to be ahead, as in two goals up

explanation.surface: Coming third in a race still wins a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third in race' reads as a finishing position but asks for a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup is a trophy awarded to winners, so it is a prize.

clue.text: Nut containers

blocks.note: first meaning: a crazy person, someone who is a wreck
second meaning: read literally, two kinds of receptacle side by side

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the clue suggests nutshells; the two words are separate definitions, the second taking the phrase as two containers.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is slang for a person who is mentally unhinged, while baskets and cases are both receptacles.

clue.text: Book outings without parking — public transport's useful

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter for parking is taken out

blocks.note: trips are outings
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a tram is a form of public transport
taken as written
handy means useful

explanation.surface: If you book trips where you cannot park, a tram comes in useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, but it is the definition: a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristram Shandy is Laurence Sterne's eighteenth-century comic novel, so it is a book.

clue.text: See 10
Od's bodikins, one that might be old hat?

indicators.note: might be signals a possible rearrangement, so the letters could form something else

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An archaic exclamation is mocked as old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Od's bodikins is an archaic minced oath, 'God's little body'; 'old hat' looks like an idiom for outdated but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Od's bodikins is an example of a mild old-fashioned curse, which is a kind of swear word or oath.

clue.text: Neo-Nazis perhaps uncomfortable with truth

blocks.note: a hard seat is uncomfortable
right is what is true or correct

explanation.surface: Neo-Nazis are uneasy with the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Neo-Nazis are an example of the far end of the political spectrum, the extreme or hard right.

clue.text: West Wing ace Sheen reportedly means to campaign

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so the actor's name is used for its sound

blocks.note: W is the compass abbreviation
a wing of a building or organisation is an arm
A is the card abbreviation for ace
a chine is a backbone or ridge, pronounced like the actor's surname

explanation.surface: Martin Sheen, star of The West Wing, is apparently using his celebrity to campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Wing looks like a single title but splits into West and Wing.
explanation.definitionFit: A war machine is the military apparatus a nation uses to wage war, the means to fight a campaign.

clue.text: Homoerotism bar is turning camper

indicators.note: bar means except or excluding, so the word is is taken out
turning means rotating and reshaping, so the remaining letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A camp gay bar is the setting, with 'camper' slyly suggesting someone more flamboyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Camper' wants to be the comparative of camp, which suits the surface; it is a holiday vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorhome is a vehicle fitted for living in, which is what a camper van is.

clue.text: Copper wearing old fur coat likely to be pardoned

indicators.note: the metal wears the coat, so the coat goes around it

blocks.note: ex means former
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
sable is a prized fur, and a sable is a coat made of it

explanation.surface: A police officer in an old fur coat hopes for a pardon.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a police officer but is the chemical element; the old fur coat is split around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An excusable fault is one that can be forgiven, so the person is likely to be pardoned.

clue.text: Ticks drawing blood?

blocks.note: surface reading: parasitic insects feeding on a host's blood
setter's reading: the rhythmic ticks of the body's pump as it draws blood through

explanation.walkthrough: Ticks look like bloodsucking bugs; they are the regular pulses of the heart, which draws in blood with each one.
explanation.definitionFit: Each beat of the heart is a tick of the body's clock, pulling blood in and pumping it out.

clue.text: Hide pieces of film in middle of reel

indicators.note: middle of asks for the central letters only of the word reel
in places one item within another, the film pieces going inside

blocks.note: the two central letters
clips are short extracts from a film

explanation.surface: An editor tucks film snippets inside a reel.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to obscure from view, as the moon hides the sun, so it means hide.

clue.text: Young socialite flipped after timber notched, perhaps

indicators.note: flipped means turned over, so the young socialite's word is read backwards

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman entering society
post is the Latin prefix meaning after

explanation.surface: A young debutante flips out after some woodwork is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: Notches on the bedpost are the traditional tally of sexual conquests, which the young socialite may have something to do with.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedpost is an upright wooden post of a bed, and lovers proverbially notch it to count conquests.

clue.text: A little merry-go-round is coming full circle

indicators.note: a little means only a small part of what follows is wanted, a run of letters inside the words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of round, the whole of is and the start of coming

explanation.surface: A short fairground ride comes back round to where it started.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a flat round shape, a solid circle rather than a ring.

clue.text: CEO a bit shaky, breaking vessel

indicators.note: something shaky is unsteady and jumbled, so these letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: the letters as written

explanation.surface: A nervous chief executive is breaking down over a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' seems to describe the shaky boss but belongs to the definition: a vessel for breaking ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceboat is another name for an icebreaker, a ship built to break a path through ice.

clue.text: DJ shortened US election day party, with vote to get in

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the vote goes inside the shortened day

blocks.note: US elections are held on a Tuesday, abbreviated Tue
a voter marks a cross on the ballot
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A disc jockey plays a short election-night party once the votes are in.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey but is dinner jacket, the British name for a tuxedo.
explanation.definitionFit: A DJ, or dinner jacket, is the British term for the formal evening jacket Americans call a tuxedo.

clue.text: Apartment full of Communist agitator's old hip bags

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so the apartment wraps around the Communist

blocks.note: a flat is an apartment
Reds are communists
a rouser stirs people up, plus the S

explanation.surface: A flat stuffed with an old Communist agitator's bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Bags is British slang for loose trousers, as in Oxford bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Flared trousers were the fashionable, hip legwear of the 1970s, and bags is a slang word for trousers.

clue.text: See 23
Stereotype of husband in loo, peeing all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The stereotypical husband in the toilet who cannot aim straight.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole someone is to put them into a fixed category, which is what stereotyping does.

clue.text: It's global but it could be British

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative, what it could otherwise be
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Something is worldwide in scope, yet might still be British.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the answer splits as 'or B.', which reads 'or British'.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, so it is globe-shaped; the orb is also part of the British crown jewels.

clue.text: Leave instruction for servant on dusty carpet?

definitions.text: instruction for servant on dusty carpet?

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang command to go away

blocks.clueFragment: instruction for servant on dusty carpet?
blocks.note: second meaning: the order to thrash the rug to knock the dust out

explanation.walkthrough: Rugs were hung on a line and struck with a carpet beater to clean them.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for go away, and literally the command to strike a rug to clean it.

clue.text: Unsuccessful immigrant lashed on return there, regularly

indicators.note: on return means coming back the other way, so the word is read in reverse
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word there is kept

blocks.note: lashed means tied with rope
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A failed immigrant was whipped on being sent back there.
explanation.definitionFit: A deportee is someone expelled from a country, an immigrant whose attempt to stay failed.
